question:
Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom.

To get out of hand
solution:
The correct answer is '**To become uncontrollable**.'

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__** 

 
• **'To get out of hand'** means to become difficult to control.

 Example: His consuming alcohol had gotten out of hand.

 
• Marked option 'To become uncontrollable' means incapable of being controlled.

 

So it is clear that the most appropriate meaning of 'To get out of hand' is 'To become uncontrollable.'

​Therefore, the correct answer is option 3.
